Chosen automatically, the model is one measured to link facts at least as precisely as words do, when one is present

control: A preservation hold (a litigation hold, an order, a claim expected) stops a matter's content being deleted, at closure or when its retention period ends: a hold on the whole matter refuses the deletion before anything changes, and records the refusal; a hold on named documents keeps those documents' originals, records and text while the rest goes; every deletion goes through one path and leaves a receipt of the SHA-256 of each original deleted, what was kept and under which hold, matched by the ledger's record of it; the matter's lead or the compliance owner places a hold with its basis and authority; only the legal or data-protection owner releases it, with identity confirmed again and a reason; the holds outlive the content (EL-004); a deletion takes with it everything the application made from the matter in its own folders (drafts and approved reports, outbox copies, evidence packs), each recorded in the receipt by its SHA-256, unless any preservation hold is in force, which keeps them all; evidence packs exported elsewhere are named in the receipt as beyond the application's control; on the Case page, Preservation holds… shows the holds in force and places or releases one
evidence: preservation_holds records; disposal receipts (artifacts/disposals/<matter>/); preservation_hold_placed / disposal_refused / content_disposed / retention_purge / preservation_hold_released events

control: Every page of a PDF is accounted for: a page that is only an image (a scan, a photographed exhibit) is read by OCR on this machine (Tesseract, after Poppler renders it, in a private temporary folder deleted afterwards) or recorded as unread; nothing is dropped without a record and a document with an unread page is never reported as wholly read. Text read by OCR carries (OCR) in its locator with the engine and the page's confidence; an unread page, or one read with less than the set confidence, holds the run until a person adds a readable copy or, having checked the original, accepts it with reasons, recorded page by page. The report states every page read by OCR, every page not read, and pages with images beside their text or with neither text nor image (EL-017); each document records the version of the reader that read it, a PDF read by an earlier version is read again from its stored original before the next run (a gap a person accepted is left as it is), a report approved before every page was accounted for is flagged by the routine checks for a new run and review, and any document can be read again from its original (Documents page, eli-legal docs --reread), for example once OCR is installed; a page with text and also images is read whole by OCR where available and what the text layer lacks is added from the image, marked (OCR, image), so an exhibit pasted under its caption is read; where OCR is not available, on a real matter such a page is a review task that holds the run; an image file (a photograph, or a scan saved as PNG, JPEG or TIFF, known by its bytes as well as its name) is read by OCR the same way, page by page for a multi-page TIFF, marked (OCR) with its confidence, or recorded unread and held, and one left unread by an earlier version is read again before the next run; on the server a document is read on a worker thread, so a long scan holds up no other session
evidence: document_processed events (OCR pages, unread pages, engine); pages_not_read / ocr_low_confidence holds and their resolutions; the report's limits

control: The server can be started from the desktop application (Settings, System) so that everyone on a case signs in from their own machine, but only by someone whose account may manage it (an administrator, a judge, a tribunal member or an arbitrator), with the passphrase again. It is the same hardened server as the command line: other machines reach it only over TLS 1.2 or later, with a self-signed certificate made if there is none and its fingerprint shown, and only with a second factor. It runs on the application's own services (one writer to the databases and the audit trail) in a thread that carries no identity, so no request can act as the person at the desktop. Each start and stop, from the application or the command line, is in the audit trail with where it listened and how it was protected; closing the application stops it.
evidence: server_started and server_stopped events (port, exposed, tls, second_factor); access_denied for anyone else

control: Case material on disk is readable only by the operating-system user running ELI Legal: its programs create everything private (umask 077), its folders are 0700 and its databases with their write-ahead files 0600, originals in the vault stay read-only (0400), and what an earlier version left readable by others is tightened at start, never following a link out of its folders. (On Windows the user's profile folder keeps others out.)
evidence: the permission bits of the data, vault and artifacts folders and of each database file

control: What is deleted is gone from the files as well as the records: the database overwrites deleted rows (secure_delete); after a matter's content is deleted its search index is merged, the database rebuilt (VACUUM) and its write-ahead log emptied; reports, outbox copies, evidence packs and vault originals ELI Legal deletes are overwritten before removal; the deletion receipt states each step. On a solid-state or copy-on-write disk old blocks can survive an overwrite: full-disk encryption covers that.
evidence: the deletion receipt's erasure block (files overwritten, database rebuilt, write-ahead log emptied); content_disposed and retention_purge events

control: How long the record is kept is chosen when ELI Legal is set up (the first-run window, or eli-legal init, which will not run unattended without it unless it is put off on purpose), the audit trail at least six months; each matter may keep its content for its own period once closed, else the organisation's. The routine checks delete a closed matter's content when its period ends (unless a preservation hold keeps it) and report an open matter idle longer than the organisation allows; a daily timer in the operating system's own scheduler (eli-legal checks timer --install) runs them when neither the application nor the server is open, catching up after the machine was off.
evidence: OA-09 compliance record (audit, closed-matter and inactivity periods); matter_updated (retention_days); retention_purge events with the period that ended; the retention check's idle-matter items

control: Papers are taken in by dropping files or whole folders on the Documents page, or by choosing them: folders are searched all the way down; hidden files, system leftovers, Office lock files and empty files are left out and the person is told which; each paper is checked before it is taken in (what it is, who filed it, who may see it, where it came from), set for all or for the selected rows at once; and reading runs in the background, as the person who filed them, with each paper counted as it is read.
evidence: document_registered and document_processed events for each paper, under the filer's name

control: A closed matter can be taken off the case list without being lost, and is never kept twice: each kind of its content (papers, analysis, reports, evidence packs: governance/retention.py) is archived into one file encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a key of its own, kept apart in the secrets folder, in parts each bound to the matter, the kind, its position and whether it is the last; each archive is opened again to prove it reads back before the working copy is overwritten and removed. Reopening the matter (its lead, with reasons and passphrase) checks every archive, every original's and every file's fingerprint, restores them and its team (anyone suspended or removed since left out and named), says what is no longer there, then destroys the archives. Destroying a kind's key, when its retention ends or by its lead's decision, makes every copy of it unreadable, backups included; a preservation hold forbids that. An archive made by 0.8.15 (one for all content) is split by kind when ELI Legal starts.
evidence: matter_closed, matter_archived (archive SHA-256, rows and files moved, encryption), matter_reopened (what was restored, access given back, who was left out), retention_purge or content_disposed with the archive destroyed and its receipt; disposal_refused under a preservation hold

control: Every case file ELI Legal keeps is encrypted on disk, whether the matter is open or closed: the original documents in the evidence vault, each version of the report and its data, the copies staged in the outbox and the evidence packs kept in its own folder are sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key per matter and kind (papers, reports, evidence packs), each file bound to its matter, kind and place, so a file moved or altered does not open; every reader checks it and the report's hash is of the plain text. Files written by an earlier version are sealed when ELI Legal starts, plain copies overwritten. Destroying a kind's key makes every copy of those files unreadable. What is handed over on purpose (an evidence pack written to a chosen folder or downloaded, a report saved as PDF or Word by a recipient) is plain where it is put, and recorded.
evidence: storage_upgraded events (originals and files sealed at start); evidence_exported (managed or handed over); disposal receipts naming the keys destroyed

control: Each kind of information is kept for its own period: the audit trail at least six months (never shortened), and from a case's closing its papers, its analysis, its reports, its evidence packs and its decision record, each set by the organisation at set-up and in Compliance (OA-09) with suggested periods and their reasons (professional rules for case papers; EU AI Act Art. 18 for documentation and Art. 26(6) for logs; Arts. 12, 14 and 19 for the decision record; GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation), the analysis and reports as long as the papers unless set otherwise, a case's papers for its own period where it has one. The routine checks retire each kind on its own day (its archive's key destroyed, or it is deleted), unless a preservation hold keeps it; the decision record goes last, only when nothing it accounts for is left, and may not be set shorter than anything it accounts for.
evidence: OA-09 compliance record with each kind's period; retention_purge events and receipts naming the kinds; record_disposed events; Closed cases showing each kind's state and end date

control: The working database (matters, documents' text, the search index, findings, reports' records) and the audit ledger are encrypted at rest with SQLCipher (AES-256 with HMAC-SHA512 per page, the write-ahead log included) under a 256-bit key made on first start and kept in the secrets folder (0600; on Windows also wrapped by the Data Protection API for the account running ELI Legal). They are opened in one place only, which refuses a wrong or missing key rather than starting an empty database. A database left plain by an earlier version is converted at the next start when nothing else has it open, the encrypted copy checked (integrity, every table's rows, the search index, the ledger's whole chain) before it replaces the plain file, which is then overwritten; an interrupted conversion is recovered. Without SQLCipher (a source checkout lacking it) the routine checks and eli-legal doctor say plainly that the databases are not encrypted. The key can be exported once for safekeeping (eli-legal database-key --out).
evidence: database_encrypted ledger event (counts only); the encryption routine check; eli-legal doctor

control: A document that could not be read is not left as a gap by default: a person entitled to decide it may describe it by hand from the original (their words become its passages, marked as theirs; the hold closes as corrected; the words are not put in the ledger) or file a readable copy (for the same party, of the same kind, seen as widely; the original's hold closes naming the copy only once the copy is read). A damaged image is reported as damaged, not as a picture with no writing.
evidence: document_described events (characters, reason; not the words); the copy's registration and the hold's resolution naming it

control: One set of live data for everyone: the server says which installation and data folder it serves (printed at start; the browser's header names the machine and installation, administrators see the folder, a developer checkout's test data is shown in red), and a developer checkout refuses to serve its test data while an installed copy's data exists unless told to (--dev-data). Every open page, desktop and browser, learns within seconds what someone else did on a case its person may see, and is drawn again (never over a form being typed or an open dialog); nothing of any other case is named.
evidence: the serve start-up lines (data folder, kind); the browser's installation chip
